newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Bank of Cyprus issue oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Cyprus issue oversubscribed.

text.p: A convertible bond issue on the Luxembourg stock exchange by the Bank of Cyprus was described as a "tremendous success" by bank officials on Wednesday, who said the 40 million pound issue was oversubscribed 3.6 times.
The issue, announced on October 21 via lead manager Salomon Brothers International, has a seven-year maturity with a call after three years and is subject to a 130 percent hurdle thereafter.
It will pay an annual coupon of 6.75 percent. The conversion premium is 15 percent. It is the first Cypriot bank to list bonds abroad.

"This success has wide-ranging implications for Cyprus and the Cypriot economy," bank chairman Solon Triantafyllides told a news conference. "It is the first time international investors from Europe and the United States have shown their faith in Cyprus and its currency."
The issue was oversubscribed with bids totalling 145 million pounds, he said.

The effect of the issue was to increase foreign investors' stake to up to nine percent of the bank's equity, Triantafyllides said, adding that the spread was such that no single investor would hold more than one percent in the bank.
Later this month Bank of Cyprus is due to issue bonds worth 10 million pounds on the local market, with preference given to current shareholders.
By May 1 it plans a 25 million pound rights issue on the Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE).
Triantafyllides said the new capital would be used to expand further in Greece. It has opened eight branches there since 1991.
